conviction_note: The H1 numbers are new: only Q1 has been published, and Q2 plus first-half profit are not out. But nothing company-level that the market has not seen turned up. The stock has re-rated about 29% on three broker upgrades since 14 Oct, with no company news, so the bar now sits above the company-compiled June consensus of £98m. Q1 retail momentum and the easy H1 comparative (H1 FY26 Retail PBT £3.5m) argue the other way. That leaves p_up near 50 (48) on a full-size move of 7%, because new numbers, a first interim under the new CEO and a possible FY27 guide nudge are all in play. The findings sum (-0.8) and the scaled number (-0.28) agree in sign. Both are small because the evidence is balanced.

already_public.what: Q1 FY27 (16 weeks to 16 Jul 2026): Group consumer revenue +3.9% to £614m, Retail +4.9% (c1% PetPlan timing benefit), Vet Group +1.9%; FY27 guidance unchanged; £25m of the £50m buyback to be complete by end of H1

FY27 guide: 'comfortable with consensus expectations for Group underlying PBT (currently £98m)'; Vets low-single-digit sales growth with profit growth; Retail market +1-2% with outperformance and PBT progress plus a one-off low-single-digit £m PetPlan exit benefit; insurance start-up costs slightly higher; capex c£50m; £50m buyback over 12 months
Company-compiled consensus FY27 underlying PBT £98m, range £90-101m, as at 10 June 2026 (not updated since)
Interim results date confirmed as 25 November 2026 on the financial calendar and in the Q1 RNS
Pets Insurance launched on Compare the Market 19 Aug 2026; targets at least 10% share in five years, break-even FY28

new_in_release.expect: Q2 and H1 (28 weeks to early Oct) sales and profit are new. Retail is lapping a very weak H1 FY26 (Retail consumer revenue -2.3%, Retail PBT £3.5m), so H1 Retail PBT should rise sharply in percentage terms; expected up, but brokers have already modelled it

FY27 PBT guide (consensus £98m, possibly higher after the Oct-Nov upgrades): most likely reiterated or nudged toward the top of £90-101m; a raise is plausible on retail momentum and the PetPlan one-off; direction unknown with a slight upward lean

First interims under CEO James Bailey, who promised in May to update 'later in the year': a strategy or medium-term framework may come with this release. Direction unknown, and it raises the size of the move
Interim dividend (policy: 50% of EPS) and start of the second £25m buyback tranche; both expected, so neutral
Retail free cash flow was -£11.1m in H1 FY26; store refresh capex c£50m; unknown

bar: FY27 Group underlying PBT £98m (range £90-101m): company-compiled consensus as at 10 June 2026, https://www.petsathomeplc.com/investors/analyst-coverage-consensus/, which the company said it was comfortable with at the prelims (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/pets-at-home-group--pets/fy26-preliminary-results-/9586476). The bar is stale: Peel Hunt (19 Oct), Jefferies (4 Nov) and Barclays (9 Nov) have since raised targets and probably estimates. No H1-specific bar was found, so the post-upgrade bar is unsourced and the findings that depend on it are capped small.
session_check: bmo. Settled from the company's own record: every prior PETS results RNS has gone out at 07:00 London (Q1 FY27 on 30 Jul 2026 07:00, FY26 prelims on 27 May 2026 07:00), and the financial calendar and the Q1 RNS both name 25 November 2026. https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/PETS
positioning_check: FCA aggregated net short 1.29% as at 2026-11-18, against 1.30% before (-0.01pp). Flat: neither building nor covering, and not crowded. https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv

findings.finding: The stock re-rated from 213.6p (14 Oct) to 275p (18 Nov), about +29%, on three sell-side moves with no company news: Peel Hunt Hold->Buy at 260p (from 180p) on 19 Oct, Jefferies 265p->305p Buy on 4 Nov, and Barclays Underweight->Equal Weight at 265p (from 180p) on 9 Nov. The bar going into the print is therefore above the June £98m consensus, and a reiterated guide risks being sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three guidance-maintained prints rose (Q3 FY26 +5.39%, FY26 prelims +6.48%, Q1 FY27 +2.39%), but each came from a depressed base of about 190-215p. This is the first print after a broker-led re-rating to a 52-week high, so there is no precedent on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced already: the 5-day tape is -4.8% (275p to 259.6p) as some of the upgrade premium bled out before the print. If the market had fully reset the bar it would read through to the company-compiled consensus, which is still June's £98m. Brokers' new estimates are not public, so the size of the gap between the old and new bar is unknown.
findings.independence: Jefferies target raise 265->305p (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-jefferies-financial-group-forecasts-strong-price-appreciation-for-pets-at-home-group-lon-pets-stock-2026-11-04/) and Barclays upgrade on 9 Nov (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/pets-at-home-stock-barclays-upgrades-rating-on-november-9/70533107) are separate documents; Yahoo daily closes confirm the price path

findings.finding: Q2 and H1 Retail are new numbers against a very soft comparative. H1 FY26 Retail consumer revenue fell 2.3% and Retail underlying PBT was £3.5m (-84%), while Q1 FY27 Retail grew +4.9% with volumes ahead of sales, so H1 Retail profit should show a large recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Retail momentum has driven the positive reactions: Q3 FY26 +5.39% and FY26 prelims +6.48% on accelerating Retail sales; Q1 FY27 +2.39% on Retail +4.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Q1 is public, and the broker upgrades cite exactly this, so it is the base case. Only the Q2 trajectory and Retail margin are unknown. If it were unpriced, the stock would not be at a 52-week high on 'improving retail volumes and margins' (Barclays).
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 RNS: Retail +4.9%, share gains, volumes ahead of sales (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/pets-at-home-group--pets/q1-fy27-trading-statement/9694643)

findings.finding: Counterparty read: CVS Group, the listed UK vet peer reporting after PETS's Q1, described a soft UK vet market. FY26 Veterinary Practice LFL was +1.0%, Q4 was hurt by extreme heat, and it gave only a 'solid start ... positive like-for-like' for Jul-Sep 2026. That is consistent with PETS's low-single-digit Vet guide (Q1 +1.9%), with no upside signal for Vets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Vets have been the steady half. The stock has moved on Retail, not on Vets, in every print since Q1 FY26 (-6.0% on 31 Jul 2025, when the Retail weakness surfaced).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it sits inside PETS's own guide of low-single-digit Vet sales growth, and CVS's results are public. It caps the size of any Vets surprise rather than signalling one.
findings.independence: PETS Q1 FY27 Vet Group +1.9% 'in line with expectations' (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/pets-at-home-group--pets/q1-fy27-trading-statement/9694643)

findings.finding: The buyback paused after the first £25m tranche (the last 'Transaction in Own Shares' RNS was 5 Oct 2026, consistent with '£25m to be complete by the end of H1'). The second £25m of the guided £50m will most likely be announced with the interims.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The capital allocation refresh at the FY26 pre-close (31 Mar 2026: a 50% payout plus the buyback) was followed by a positive prelims reaction (+6.48%). There is no isolated reaction to a buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: Guided in May ('We will complete a £50m buyback over the next 12 months'), so the restart is expected. A larger programme would be new, but there is no evidence for one.

findings.finding: Pets Insurance launched on 19 Aug 2026 (Compare the Market first, own channels in September), underwritten by Great Lakes. Start-up costs were guided 'slightly higher in FY27' with break-even targeted for FY28, so H1 carries launch losses.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no isolated reaction: the insurance loss widened from £3m to £5m at the FY26 interims, which rose +4.83% on other lines.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside guidance, so mostly priced. The only unpriced part is early customer take-up, which could be framed either way.
findings.independence: Insurance Times on the 10% share target (https://www.insurancetimes.co.uk/news/pets-at-home-chases-at-least-10-market-share-after-entering-insurance/1459431.article)

baseline_tension: The priced lean is +0.46 (short_squeeze 0.77 on a non-crowded 1.29% short, run-up -0.34) and the 20/60-day run-up is +6.8%/+22%. The upgrade-driven re-rating finding cuts against that run-up (negative), while the Retail recovery agrees with it, so the set is near-balanced and slightly negative, below the lean.
language_note: The UK local half here is the RNS record (Investegate) and the company's own IR site, not a second language. They carried the company-compiled consensus (£98m, range £90-101m, dated 10 June), the pause in buyback RNS after 5 Oct, and the confirmed 25 Nov date; the English wire and aggregator sources carried the broker upgrades. No domestic retail-investor source (Sharecast, Proactive, IC) was reachable, so nothing beyond that.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': cut the H1 Retail finding from +0.8 to +0.5, because Q1 is pre-released and only Q2 and the margin are new

'The move is in the guide' / 'too small about the move': raised abs_move_pct from 6.0 to 7.0, because the H1 numbers are not pre-released, a first interim under a new CEO with a promised update is likely, and an FY27 guide nudge is plausible; p_up held at 48
'Coverage tells you which regime you are in': 12 analysts on the IR list (the well-covered band), so p_up stays near 50 rather than moving on inference
